newsitem.title: USA: U.S.stocks seen firming at open after GDP data.
newsitem.headline: U.S.stocks seen firming at open after GDP data.

text.p: U.S. stocks were seen getting support at the opening on Friday from market-friendly revised fourth quarter gross domestic product (GDP) data.

Analysts earlier had predicted a lower opening following Thursday's battering of high technology stocks. But the GDP data could be enough to support a higher opening, although stocks did not appear posed for a sharp rally, they said.

"I would guess that since the number is not a piece of negative news, the market may attempt a bit of a rally today once we can get the tech stocks to turn," said Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood.
Fourth quarter gross domestic product data was revised to a rise of 3.9 percent from a 4.7 percent rise in the preliminary estimate. Economists expected the number to be up 4.1 percent.
"There's no indication that significant inflationary pressures are playing a role in the economy at this time," said Alan Ackerman, senior vp and market strategist, Fahnestock and Co.
